copy.tagline: Federally subsidized cash flow in a tightening Pittsburgh market.
copy.thesis: A 200-unit HAP-contract community on the Pittsburgh airport corridor, acquired at $149K/unit. Project-based Section 8 anchors in-place income while a $2.5M interior and common-area renovation lifts NOI from roughly $1.05M in the partial first year to a stabilized $1.5M+. The entry basis sits at a sub-5% stabilized cap against 5.78% agency debt, so this is a cash-flow-and-preservation hold rather than a cap-rate-compression play; the base case underwrites a conservative 6.25% exit.

marketFindings.headline: Pittsburgh vacancy tightening toward 4% as rent growth accelerates to 3.8%
marketFindings.body: Northmarq reports Pittsburgh apartment vacancy ending 2025 around 4.5% — matching its five-year average — with rent growth forecast to accelerate to 3.8% by year-end and stay positive through 2026 as demand outpaces a moderating supply pipeline. Pittsburgh remains a national outperformer versus oversupplied Sun Belt metros.

marketFindings.headline: Older value-add vintage is exactly what Pittsburgh buyers want
marketFindings.body: Properties built in the 1950s and 1970s account for nearly 25% of Pittsburgh multifamily transactions, and in-place cap rates for quality assets with value-add upside have run 5.5%–6.0%. Our 1979-vintage asset at a $2.5M renovation basis sits squarely in the most actively traded segment of this market.

marketFindings.headline: Nearly 600 new jobs and $109M landing in Coraopolis
marketFindings.body: Mainspring Energy is building a 292,000 SF clean-tech manufacturing plant in the Northfield Industrial Park in Findlay Township/Coraopolis on Allegheny County Airport Authority land, backed by $8.6M in state incentives — creating at least 597 jobs. It anchors a broader airport-corridor employment base that supports workforce-housing demand nearby.

sources.title: Shapiro Administration Invests $8.6M to Recruit Mainspring Energy, Creating Nearly 600 Jobs in Allegheny County — PA.gov

marketFindings.headline: FY2026 appropriations sustain Section 8 project-based rental assistance
marketFindings.body: The FY2026 HUD appropriations bill continues funding for renewal of Section 8 project-based rental assistance (PBRA) contracts — the operating subsidy that anchors this property's in-place income — and HUD published FY2026 Annual Adjustment Factors effective December 9, 2025 that escalate HAP contract rents. Federal subsidy continuity underpins the base-case cash flow.

marketFindings.headline: Entry basis prices in cap-rate expansion risk
marketFindings.body: At $149K/unit the going-in yield on stabilized NOI is roughly 4.9%, inside the 5.5%–6.0% range where comparable Pittsburgh value-add trades. Buying at ~4.9% against 5.78% debt is negative leverage, and a 6.25% exit puts sale value below the entry price — so the base case leans on subsidized cash flow and debt paydown, not appreciation. Minimum operating-year DSCR is 0.81, indicating the senior loan is undersized against in-place NOI.
